source_evidence: interest rates that are periodically re-set through auctions, typically every 7, 14, 28, or 35 days
answer: Auction Rate Securities (ARS) have interest rates that reset periodically through auctions rather than staying at one rate indefinitely. These auctions typically occur every 7, 14, 28, or 35 days. The auction is intended to establish a clearing rate; if too few bidders participate, it may fail to establish one.
